investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or pool limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or pool limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
